does_geometry_mechanically_change_the_sc.evidence: FAR > NEAR in 24/24 descendant pairs; FAR/NEAR ratio min 1.1461, median 1.4058, max 1.6876
does_geometry_mechanically_change_the_sc.reading: the FAR arm drifts more on its own sham, so it buys a systematically larger TAU. A_X[b] sums both arms, so the per-ancestry gate is set predominantly by the noisier arm. This is a mechanical property of the rule, not an outcome.

does_allocation_mechanically_change_the_.evidence: within NEAR, TAU(a=1) > TAU(a=0) in 12/12 ancestries; within FAR the ordering flips (5/12), i.e. no consistent direction
does_allocation_mechanically_change_the_.why_it_does_not_threaten_the_rule: A_X[b] is a symmetric sum over both allocation members, so A_X and A_X_BAR are exactly invariant under allocation exchange (proved separately). The per-descendant asymmetry is descriptive only.

scaling_with_contrast_arity.A_X[b]: a SUM of the four cell TAU values, scaled by 1/sqrt(2). It GROWS LINEARLY with the number of cells entering the contrast: adding cells raises the gate, it does not lower it.
scaling_with_contrast_arity.A_X_BAR: a MEAN over ancestries of per-ancestry gates. It is INVARIANT in the number of independent ancestries: adding ancestries does not shrink it.
scaling_with_contrast_arity.value_if_it_were_a_standard_error: a sampling envelope would shrink as 1/sqrt(12) to 8.440995773e-04; the realized A_X_BAR is 2.924046709e-03, i.e. it does not shrink at all
scaling_with_contrast_arity.consistency_verdict: CONSISTENT WITH A MINIMUM-EFFECT GATE, NOT WITH A SAMPLING UNCERTAINTY. A sampling standard error shrinks with n; a declared minimum-effect scale does not. The record's aggregation across ancestries is itself a worst-case L1 step, so the conservatism is applied twice: once over the eight rows of one ancestry, once over the twelve ancestries.
